title: The fog line race
body: Climb the Vulcan steps before 8 AM and stop exactly where the fog turns into blue sky. Take one photo facing each direction without moving your feet.

title: The no-escalator commute
body: Start at the bottom of the 16th Avenue steps just after sunrise. Reach the top without pausing, then walk down the parallel street without looking back.

title: Three hills, one song
body: Pick one song longer than seven minutes and start it at the base of Billy Goat Hill. Reach the rope swing overlook before it ends.

title: The stairway with no street
body: Find the Pemberton steps before the neighborhood wakes up. Climb every flight, but turn around only at landings with a view.

title: The concrete slide circuit
body: Bring cardboard to the Seward slides on a dry weekday morning. Take exactly three runs, making each one quieter than the last.

title: The creek you can almost hear
body: Enter Glen Canyon after rain and follow the lowest trail for twenty minutes. Stop wherever traffic disappears and count five separate bird calls.

title: The midnight switchbacks
body: Walk the Harry Street steps after 9 PM with one friend. At every landing, trade who leads without saying why.

title: The wind test
body: Cross the Bernal rock labyrinth on the windiest afternoon you can find. Keep one hand in your pocket the entire way.

title: The hidden tennis warm-up
body: Reach the little court at Douglass Park before 7 AM. Rally until someone hits the fence, then leave immediately.

title: The eucalyptus sprint
body: Enter Mount Sutro when the fog is thick enough to bead on your sleeves. Power-walk to the summit and do not check the map twice.

title: The crooked block climb
body: Start at the bottom of Vermont Street at blue hour. Walk its curves backward while your friend watches for cars.

title: The tide-line dash
body: At low tide, walk the narrow strip below Heron's Head as far as dry shoes allow. Race the returning water back to the path.

title: The reservoir lap with rules
body: Circle the Upper Reservoir at golden hour. Jog the sunny side, walk the shadow side, and switch every time a dog passes.

title: The industrial shoreline mile
body: Start at Warm Water Cove before the lunch trucks arrive. Walk south until you find three different warning signs, then retrace the route faster.

title: The dune crossing
body: Enter the Presidio dunes just after a windy night. Follow only footprints that are already fading and leave no straight path of your own.

title: The dawn pier count
body: Reach Pier 70 before sunrise and walk every public edge you can find. Count cranes, not boats, and turn back at twelve.

title: The last bench before dark
body: Reach the bench above Tank Hill fifteen minutes before sunset. Sit until the city lights outnumber the people, and keep your phones in your pockets.

title: The library's smallest window
body: Go to the Potrero branch during the last hour before closing. Find the seat with the narrowest view and read ten pages of something chosen from the returns cart.

title: The quiet side of the reservoir
body: Reach Pine Lake before 9 AM and sit on the side without a path. Stay until you see the same bird land twice.

title: The greenhouse rain room
body: Visit the tiny greenhouse at Alemany Farm while it is raining. Listen from under the awning for ten minutes before stepping inside.

title: The blue-hour bleachers
body: Sit on the highest empty bleacher at Palega just after sunset. Each person names one window they think has the best life behind it.

title: The eucalyptus weather report
body: Lie beneath the trees at Interior Greenbelt on a foggy afternoon. Decide what the weather sounds like without using any weather words.

title: The empty amphitheater
body: Find the stone seats at McLaren's Jerry Garcia Amphitheater before noon on a weekday. Sit in three different rows and choose which one makes silence sound largest.

title: The ferry wake watch
body: Stand at India Basin after the afternoon wind starts. Watch five boat wakes arrive without checking which boat made them.

title: The two-cup thermos
body: Bring one thermos to Esprit Park at 7 AM and two cups. Pour both before either person speaks.

title: The garden after closing time
body: Reach the gate of the Cayuga playground garden ten minutes before dusk. Walk the outside fence and pick a carved face to remember without photographing it.

title: The hill that faces away
body: Sit on the east slope of Kite Hill at sunset, facing away from downtown. Leave only when the grass stops looking green.

title: The laundromat intermission
body: Start a wash cycle at a neighborhood laundromat after 8 PM. Spend the whole cycle outside on the nearest bench with no headphones.

title: The secret picnic table
body: Find the single table behind Sunnyside Conservatory on a weekday afternoon. Bring one fruit neither person has eaten this month.

title: The fog bell pause
body: Stand near the Fort Mason piers when the foghorns begin. Close your eyes for three signals, then point toward the one that sounded farthest away.

title: The after-rain overlook
body: Visit Brooks Park within an hour after the rain stops. Sit where the grass is still dry and watch the clouds leave before you do.

title: The midnight book exchange
body: Take a book you are finished with to a sidewalk library after 10 PM. Leave it, take nothing, and read the handwritten notes inside three others.

title: The color nobody frames
body: Find the most sun-faded door on Balmy Alley after a rainy morning. Photograph only its shadow, then compare it with the door itself.

title: Twelve shades of concrete
body: Walk the Islais Creek edge at noon, when the light is least flattering. Make a twelve-photo grid using only concrete and water.

title: The upside-down skyline
body: Go to a puddled street in Dogpatch after rain. Photograph the skyline only through reflections and never point the camera above your waist.

title: The accidental alphabet
body: Walk one block of Mission Street before 8 AM. Find five letters made by fire escapes, wires, or shadows—no printed signs allowed.

title: The orange window
body: Reach the Bernal Cut at golden hour. Frame the same passing train through three different gaps in the fence.

title: The one-color market
body: Enter Alemany Market in its final hour. Pick one color and photograph it seven times without capturing a face.

title: The shadow staircase
body: Reach the Lincoln Park steps when the sun is low. Photograph the stairs without including a single tile—shadows only.

title: The smallest skyline
body: Find a view of downtown through a chain-link opening at Potrero del Sol. Make the whole skyline fit inside one diamond.

title: The night bus triptych
body: Ride the 24 for exactly three stops after 9 PM. At each stop, photograph the same empty seat from a different angle.

title: The painted utility hunt
body: Walk Precita Avenue on a foggy morning and find four utility boxes painted in incompatible styles. Frame them as if they belong together.

title: The red-light portrait
body: Stand beneath the old neon at the 500 Club after dark. Make a portrait using only reflected red light—keep the sign outside the frame.

title: The invisible playground
body: Visit the hand-built corners of Cayuga just after sunrise. Photograph five carved faces without showing the object each face belongs to.

title: The windy still life
body: Bring three light objects to Candlestick Point on a windy afternoon. Arrange and photograph them before the wind changes the composition.

title: The garage geometry
body: Enter the public stairwell at the Fifth and Mission garage before the evening rush. Make three abstract photos without showing a car.

title: The single lit window
body: Climb Ina Coolbrith after blue hour. Photograph one lit window across the city while keeping every nearer window dark.

title: The tide erases it
body: Draw a tiny shape at the edge of Ocean Beach during an incoming tide. Photograph it once per wave until it is gone.

title: The bakery's first mistake
body: Arrive at a neighborhood bakery within fifteen minutes of opening. Ask what came out misshapen and take whatever they point to.

title: The unlabeled soda
body: Go to a corner store after 8 PM and choose a drink whose flavor you cannot identify from the label. Split it three ways and vote before looking it up.

title: The last dumpling rule
body: Order one unfamiliar dumpling per person just before the lunch rush ends. Nobody can claim the last piece; settle it with rock-paper-scissors.

title: The five-dollar picnic
body: Each person gets five dollars at the Alemany market in its last hour. Build one shared picnic without buying the same color twice.

title: The pastry compass
body: Buy one pastry you have never tried on a foggy morning. Walk in the direction its pointed end faces and eat it at the first bench.

title: The menu blind spot
body: At a family diner before 9 AM, order the breakfast item printed in the smallest type. Trade exactly one bite with your friend.

title: The bus-stop dessert
body: Buy one cold dessert after sunset and eat it at the next bus shelter, even if no bus is coming. Rate only the shelter's ambiance.

title: The mystery herb
body: Visit a produce market in the final hour and buy the herb you recognize least. Smell it on the walk home and build dinner around it.

title: The warm tortilla timer
body: Arrive at the tortilleria before noon and buy the smallest stack. Eat one plain before it stops steaming; save the rest for someone else.

title: The one-block progressive dinner
body: On one block after 6 PM, get a snack, a drink, and something sweet from three different counters. You cannot sit down between stops.

title: The off-menu color
body: Ask for the brightest thing the kitchen can make without naming an ingredient. Share it, and guess the dominant flavor before anyone speaks to the server again.

title: The bread-end rescue
body: Visit a bakery thirty minutes before closing and ask whether any bread ends need a home. Take them to the nearest overlook with one good spread.

title: The freezer-door oracle
body: At a small market after 9 PM, let the foggiest freezer door choose your snack. Buy the first item visible when the glass clears.

title: The soup weather pact
body: Wait for a day below 55 degrees, then order the soup with the fewest English words in its description. Eat it outside anyway.

title: The two-neighborhood sandwich
body: Buy bread on one side of Mission Street and the filling on the other before noon. Assemble the sandwich at Precita Park with no utensils.

title: The final tray bet
body: Reach a dim sum bakery in the last hour. Each person silently points to the final item they think will sell out; split whichever one disappears first.

title: The house with a second face
body: Walk the Sunnyside side streets at dusk until you find a house that looks like a face. Give it a name, but do not photograph it.

title: The public phone séance
body: Find a surviving payphone after dark. Pick it up, listen for ten seconds, and leave a voicemail for your future self from your real phone.

title: The city's smallest parade
body: Bring three objects that make different sounds to an empty block before 7 AM. March them from one corner to the next and stop when a window opens.

title: The wrong-way viewpoint
body: Reach Grandview before sunset, then face the least impressive direction. Convince your friend it is the best view in the city.

title: The anonymous monument
body: Find a plaque in McLaren Park that neither person understands. Invent the event it commemorates and deliver a thirty-second speech.

title: The midnight chess problem
body: Draw an eight-square chessboard in sidewalk chalk after 10 PM. Play a game using found objects and leave the losing king behind.

title: The echo census
body: Enter the pedestrian tunnel under Bosworth after the evening rush. Test five sounds and rank their echoes without using your voice.

title: The borrowed constellation
body: Lie on the grass at Holly Park after 9 PM. Connect five lit apartment windows into a constellation and name it after a group-chat joke.

title: The staircase prophecy
body: Climb the Farnsworth steps on a windy day. At each landing, write down the first word you hear; read the sentence only at the top.

title: The tiny door census
body: Walk one block of Noe Valley just after sunrise and count every door too small for a person. Stop at seven, even if the block is unfinished.

title: The fog exchange
body: Bring a sealed note to Mount Davidson when the summit is hidden in fog. Trade notes with your friend without reading them until you are below the cloud.

title: The fence museum
body: Choose a block in Bayview at midday and curate a five-piece museum made entirely of things caught in fences. Give the tour in a whisper.

title: The pigeon committee
body: Sit near a quiet plaza at lunch and assign every pigeon a job title. Leave when the CEO flies away.

title: The invisible boundary
body: Walk from the Mission into Bernal at blue hour. Each person silently decides where the neighborhood changed; compare answers only after crossing Cortland.

title: The reverse time capsule
body: Find something harmless on the sidewalk that looks ten years old. Write a note explaining today to it, photograph both, then take only the note home.

title: The one-person audience
body: Go to the outdoor stage at Cayuga before 8 AM. Perform one minute of anything for exactly one carved wooden figure.
